I read "Unassigned" as an assertion about the organization, not an absence of evidence, so I count it as invented. A more lenient reading would take it as "not yet named in this assessment" and pass the case.
The other characterizations are labeled assumptions or follow from the input: "high-risk-like use" follows from hiring, and "Candidates will be affected" is labeled as an assumption.

However, it presents all twelve RACI roles as "Unassigned" and repeats this in the open items. That states an absence about the organization's ownership that the input never gives. The ruling treats this as an invented fact because it is neither labeled as an assumption nor phrased as an absence of evidence. The "Unknown: insufficient data" label would have been the correct form for owners. This triggers the fail indicator, so the verdict is FAIL.
